author: Ava Brendgord
title: TXST kicks off fall semester with enrollment growth and Pac-12 buzz - NewsBreak
text:
By Ava Brendgord ,
11 hours ago
SAN MARCOS, Texas (KXAN) -- Texas State University's first day back to class comes with record-setting growth and a new era of Pac-12 football on the horizon.
While the numbers are unofficial until a few weeks into the school year, TXST expects over 47,000 bobcats on campus this fall, continuing its streak as the fastest-growing university in the state.
"By this time next year, we will be over 50,000 students or so," university president Dr. Kelly Damphousse said. "A lot of people want to come to Texas State."
Dr. Kelly Damphousse (Todd Bailey/ KXAN) Most noticeable on campus, construction work on two new residential towers called Juniper and Verbena Halls. The dorms are near the LBJ Student Center and the Alkek Library. It's just one of many construction projects underway this school year.
Construction at Texas State University on August 19, 2026. (Todd Bailey/KXAN) "Currently, we have about 10,000 beds on campus, but we'll be at 12,000 beds this time next year. We held it down this year just because we were running out of beds, but we will take off again next year," Damphousse said.
Garnering the most buzz, the bobcat's first season in the Pac-12 Conference after more than a decade in the Sun Belt Conference.
It comes after the university’s decision to approve a $5 million exit fee to leave the Sun Belt and join the Pac-12 alongside Oregon State, Washington State, Boise State, Colorado State, Fresno State, San Diego State, Utah State, and Gonzaga, who joined the conference as a non-football member.
"I think it's cool. I feel like the energy's going to be up in the stadium," Isaiah Phoenix, a freshman from Hutto, told KXAN on his way to class.
First day of class at Texas State University. (Todd Bailey/ KXAN) "I'm a part of the drumline here, so I think it will be cool seeing the big crowds and stuff, especially in this new conference," Phoenix's buddy Luke Cart added.
Damphousse called the move an exciting, yet different experience, and he's happy to join the historic conference.
"We excited about the locations we're going to and the schools that will be coming here. I think our fans are super excited about going on the road with our football team, which has never really happened before, so that will be a lot of fun," he said.
